requirements.requirement: Limit datauser account to 100MB of storage under /srv/data on node1, enforced by the filesystem itself
requirements.summary: datauser was created, an XFS-backed loopback filesystem was mounted at /srv/data with the usrquota option, and xfs_quota was used to set bsoft=bhard=102400 blocks (100MB) for datauser. Live enforcement was directly demonstrated: an 80MB write succeeded, and a subsequent write correctly failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' once usage hit exactly 100MB. The configuration (fstab entry, quota limits, mount options) persists and enforcement was re-verified identically after a full node reboot, confirming durable, kernel-enforced (not application-level) limiting.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1 (independent check)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id 646e5f74..., mount/quota/fstab/user state) was captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, connectivity loss confirmed the node went down, a different post-restart boot_id (e899d591...) was observed matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, and post-restart state showed the mount restored via fstab, quota configuration intact, and live enforcement still functioning.

overall_summary: The task was completed and directly verified: datauser is limited to 100MB under /srv/data via an XFS user quota (bsoft=bhard=100m) enforced by the kernel, with live write tests confirming the hard limit both before and after a full node reboot. Given the constraint that the root filesystem is a single XFS partition without a dedicated /srv mount, the executor's loopback-image approach is a reasonable and valid implementation choice for filesystem-enforced quotas. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also satisfied with a clean pre/post boot-identity transition and recovered service state. Hygiene is good overall; the only blemishes are a quickly self-corrected mount-option mistake and one small leftover log file.
limitations: Root disk usage (df -hT /) before/after was not explicitly re-captured post-reboot, so total disk consumption from the 300MB backing image over time is not directly confirmed, though this is a minor completeness gap given quota enforcement itself was directly verified.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled for this task), so no separate prepare-phase state could be distinguished from executor changes; all changes are attributable to the executor by default.

operational_hygiene.summary: Almost all state-changing commands map directly to task fulfillment (user creation, backing image, mount, quota configuration) or bounded verification that was cleaned up (test files written then removed both pre- and post-reboot). One early mount attempt used an invalid xfs mount option ('uquotaenforce'), causing a failed mount (cmd-e95ee33a5aca494c, rc=32) and a transient incorrect fstab line; this was immediately corrected in the very next command (cmd-5dbefd13e0a14347) with no lasting effect on the final configuration, so it is treated as a minor, low-risk, self-corrected misstep rather than unwanted residue. The reboot (cmd-2e034e74b126436c) is an expected part of the restart-evidence protocol. One small residual artifact remains: /tmp/reboot.log, created as the redirect target for the backgrounded reboot command, appears in the after_executor temporary-files listing and was not cleaned up; this is low-risk and expected from the nohup pattern but is technically leftover state.
